title: Sell Mineral Rights in Shirley, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Shirley, AR
metaDescription: Shirley, AR mineral rights in Van Buren County, one of the original Fayetteville Shale core counties. Legacy leases from the 2004-era discovery.
heroLead: Van Buren County is where the Fayetteville Shale story effectively began, and Shirley sits inside the same corridor where Southwestern Energy proved the play could work as a horizontal shale gas field.
intro: The Fayetteville Shale's initial discovery wells in the early 2000s were drilled in this part of central Arkansas, and Van Buren County quickly became one of the play's most heavily developed areas. Land around Shirley has been part of that story from the beginning, and mineral ownership here often carries some of the longest production histories in the entire play.

sections.heading: Ground Zero for the Play
paragraphs: Because Van Buren County was central to proving out the Fayetteville Shale as a commercial horizontal gas play, drilling density around Shirley has historically been among the highest anywhere in the field. Many local mineral interests have a production record going back close to two decades, now well into the long, low-decline phase typical of mature shale wells.

sections.heading: Long Histories, Sometimes Complicated Records
paragraphs: With nearly twenty years of activity, some Shirley-area leases have been assigned between operators multiple times, and units have occasionally been reconfigured as development matured. None of that is unusual for a field this established, and it doesn't prevent a sale, but it does mean title work sometimes takes a bit more tracing than in a less-developed area.

faqs.question: Is Shirley part of the original Fayetteville Shale discovery area?
faqs.answer: Yes, Van Buren County was central to the early development that proved the play, and Shirley sits within that historically active corridor.

faqs.question: My lease has been reassigned to a different operator over the years. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: No, multiple assignments are common for leases this old and don't prevent a sale once current ownership and operator status are confirmed.

faqs.question: How much longer might a well from the original boom keep producing?
faqs.answer: Many original-era Fayetteville Shale wells continue producing at low volumes well past the fifteen-year mark, though the exact remaining life varies by well.

faqs.question: What makes evaluating a Shirley-area interest different from a newer part of the play?
faqs.answer: A longer history means more data points, more potential title complexity from repeated assignments, and generally a clearer picture of long-term decline behavior for a buyer to work from.

faqs.question: Should I expect a Van Buren County interest to be worth more given the area's history?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. History gives a buyer more data to work with, but value still depends on remaining production, lease terms, and comparable recent transactions rather than the area's reputation alone.
